name: Pulmonary Nodular Lymphoid Hyperplasia
aliases: Nodular Lymphoid Hyperplasia of the Lung

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Pulmonary Nodular Lymphoid Hyperplasia Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of benign lymphoid proliferation with reactive germinal centers in lung tissue
Presence of solitary or multiple well-defined pulmonary nodules on chest imaging without evidence of malignancy
Exclusion of lymphoma, other lymphoproliferative disorders, and infectious causes by clinical, histological, and microbiological evaluation
Clinical stability or slow progression without systemic symptoms suggestive of malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus compatible radiologic findings and exclusion of malignancy and infection
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, radiology, and clinical correlation.

searchTerms: nodular lung pattern on high-res CT

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
Absence of monoclonal lymphoid populations on flow cytometry
imaging: Well-circumscribed solitary or multiple pulmonary nodules on chest X-ray or CT scan
No evidence of cavitation or aggressive features
other: Histopathology showing reactive lymphoid follicles with germinal centers and polyclonal lymphoid cells

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss and night sweats
Presence of infectious organisms on microbiological studies

redFlags: Systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Evidence of monoclonal lymphoid proliferation on biopsy
references: Cordier JF. Pulmonary nodular lymphoid hyperplasia. Eur Respir J. 1993;6(5):737-740.
Katzenstein AL, Fiorelli RF. Nodular lymphoid hyperplasia of the lung. Am J Surg Pathol. 1983;7(7):547-553.
Orphanet: Pulmonary Nodular Lymphoid Hyperplasia. ORPHA:60026.
